'''Nathan Sharon''' ({{langx|he|נתן שרון}}; November 1925<ref name="Symp">[http://www.weizmann.ac.il/conferences/Nsharon/new_pages/invitation.html Symposium at the Weizmann Institute of Science entitled: "Half a Century at the Carbohydrate-Protein Interface" - Invitation] 23/24 November 2005, accessed 21 June 2011</ref> &ndash; 17 June 2011<ref name="Avalim">[http://www.avelim.co.il/archives/18946  "Prof. Nathan Sharon dec'd"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110904190109/http://www.avelim.co.il/archives/18946 |date=4 September 2011 }}.  ''Avalim'' Notices (in Hebrew), 19 June 2011</ref>) was an Israeli [[biochemist]].

==Biography==
Sharon was born in 1925 in [[Brest, Belarus|Brest-Litovsk]], then part of [[Poland]] (now Brest, [[Belarus]]). He [[Aliyah|emigrated]] to [[Mandatory Palestine|Mandate Palestine]] with his family in 1934 and settled in [[Tel Aviv]].<ref name="palmach">[http://www.palmach.org.il/show_item.asp?levelId=38495&itemId=6316&itemType=0&fighter=73133 CV of Nathan Sharon (in Hebrew)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120318074747/http://www.palmach.org.il/show_item.asp?levelId=38495&itemId=6316&itemType=0&fighter=73133 |date=18 March 2012 }} Palmach web site</ref> Concurrent with his high school studies, Sharon joined the [[Gadna (Israel)|Gadna]] military youth program in 1941, and following his graduation from school, in 1943, he joined the [[Palmach]], serving until 1945.<ref name="palmach"/>

During the [[1948 Arab–Israeli War]], Sharon served in the Science Corps of the [[Israel Defense Forces]], attaining the rank of lieutenant colonel, and he focused his work on the development of gas flame throwers.<ref name="palmach"/>

Sharon studied chemistry at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]]. In 1950, he graduated and, in 1953, he was awarded a doctorate.<ref name="palmach"/>

In 1954, he joined the faculty of the Department for Biophysics at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]], headed by professor [[Ephraim Katzir]], where he became a professor in 1968. In 1974, he was appointed head of the department, a position he held intermittently until his retirement in 1990. He also served as dean of the Faculty of Chemistry and Physics and was a visiting professor at [[Harvard University|Harvard]], [[University of Oxford|Oxford]] universities and the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref name="palmach"/> He was also a member of the senate of the [[Open University of Israel]] and a member of the council of the Tel Aviv-Yafo Academic College.<ref name="Avalim"/> He served as editor of "World of Science" broadcast on [[Israel Radio]], editor of the journal "''Mada''" (Science) and science and technology editor of the ''[[Haaretz]]'' newspaper.<ref name="palmach"/>

He was a leading figure in the research of [[carbohydrate]] and [[glycoprotein]] for more than fifty years.<ref name="Symp"/> He authored several seminal works on [[lectins]] and [[glycoconjugates]], including the discovery of lectins, their interactions with carbohydrates, and their subsequent use in laboratory research and diagnostics.<ref>[Jeremiah Silbert. Lectins: Personal Comments of Nathan Sharon Taken from his Memoirs (Translation from Hebrew). From Antitumor Potential and other Emerging Medicinal Properties of Natural Compounds. Edited by Fang EF. Ng TB].</ref><ref name="dadamo">{{Cite web |url=http://www.drpeterjdadamo.com/wiki/wiki.pl/Nathan_Sharon#Nathan_Sharon2 |title=''The Individualist'' profile of Nathan Sharon |access-date=21 June 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101213114244/http://www.drpeterjdadamo.com/wiki/wiki.pl/Nathan_Sharon#Nathan_Sharon2 |archive-date=13 December 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 1992, he was elected to the [[Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities]].<ref name="Avalim"/><ref name="palmach"/>

He died on 17 June 2011 at the age of 85.<ref>[http://glycob.oxfordjournals.org/content/21/9/1119.full Obituary: Nathan Sharon, 1925–2011]</ref>

==Honours and awards==
Sharon received numerous honorary degrees and awards including: 
*1987: Weizmann Prize for Sciences.
*1987: Honorary doctorate from the [[University of Paris]].<ref name="palmach"/>
*1989: Bijvoet Medal of the [[Bijvoet Center for Biomolecular Research]], Utrecht University, NL<ref>{{cite web|url=http://bijvoet-center.eu/bijvoet-medal/|title=Bijvoet Medal|publisher=Bijvoet Center for Biomolecular Research|accessdate=2017-09-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170912191415/http://bijvoet-center.eu/bijvoet-medal/|archive-date=12 September 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>
*1994: [[Israel Prize]] in biochemistry.<ref name=prize>{{Cite web|title=Israel Prize Official Site - Recipients in 1994 (in Hebrew)|url=http://cms.education.gov.il/EducationCMS/Units/PrasIsrael/TashnagTashsab/TASNAG_TASNAT_Rikuz.htm?DictionaryKey=Tashnad}}</ref>

==Family==
Sharon married Rachel (Itzikson) in 1948 and has two daughters, Esther (Esty) Sharon, and Osnat Bairey.<ref name="Avalim"/><ref name="palmach"/>

He was the nephew of [[Pinchas Sapir]], the former [[Finance Minister of Israel|Israeli Finance Minister]] and the brother of [[Shmuel Shtrikman]], who was awarded the 2001 Israel Prize for physics.<ref>{{Cite web| title = Israel Prize Official Site (in Hebrew) – Award to Shmuel Shtrikman - Judges' Rationale| url = http://cms.education.gov.il/EducationCMS/Units/PrasIsrael/Tashsa/ShmuelShtikerman/NimokyHsoftim.htm}}</ref>

==Selected works==
Sharon published over 400 papers in international scientific journals and wrote or edited eight books in English and Hebrew.<ref name="palmach"/> His published works include: 
* ''Lectins'', co-authored with Halina Lis (Kluwer Academic Publishers, 2003 (2nd edition)).
